checks.title: Root account has MFA enabled
checks.rationale: Root MFA is the single most important control for an AWS account.
checks.remediation: Console > Security credentials > Activate MFA on the root user; prefer hardware MFA.

checks.title: Root account access keys are absent
checks.rationale: Root access keys are nearly never needed and represent total-account compromise risk.
checks.remediation: Delete all access keys for the root user in IAM > Security credentials.

checks.title: IAM password policy requires minimum length >= 14
checks.rationale: CIS recommends a 14+ character minimum to resist offline cracking.
checks.remediation: aws iam update-account-password-policy --minimum-password-length 14.

checks.title: IAM password policy enforces symbol + number + mixed case
checks.command: aws iam get-account-password-policy --output json 2>/dev/null | python -c "import sys,json; p=json.load(sys.stdin)['PasswordPolicy']; print(all([p.get('RequireSymbols'), p.get('RequireNumbers'), p.get('RequireUppercaseCharacters'), p.get('RequireLowercaseCharacters')]))"
checks.rationale: Complexity policy raises the work factor for password guessing.
checks.remediation: aws iam update-account-password-policy --require-symbols --require-numbers --require-uppercase-characters --require-lowercase-characters.

checks.title: CloudTrail multi-region trail exists
checks.rationale: A multi-region trail is the foundation of AWS audit logging.
checks.remediation: aws cloudtrail create-trail --name <name> --s3-bucket-name <bucket> --is-multi-region-trail --enable-log-file-validation.

checks.title: CloudTrail log file validation enabled
checks.rationale: Log-file validation produces digest files used to detect tampering.
checks.remediation: aws cloudtrail update-trail --name <name> --enable-log-file-validation.

checks.title: S3 Account Public Access Block: all four flags TRUE
checks.command: aws s3control get-public-access-block --account-id $(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text 2>/dev/null) --output json 2>/dev/null | python -c "import sys,json; c=json.load(sys.stdin)['PublicAccessBlockConfiguration']; print(all(c.values()))"
checks.rationale: Account-level Block Public Access overrides per-bucket misconfiguration.
checks.remediation: aws s3control put-public-access-block --account-id <id> --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true.

checks.title: Default VPC security groups in scanned region disallow all inbound
checks.command: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=group-name,Values=default --query 'SecurityGroups[?length(IpPermissions)>`0`] | length(@)' --output text 2>/dev/null
checks.rationale: The default SG should be locked down; resources should attach to scoped SGs.
checks.remediation: aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress and aws ec2 revoke-security-group-egress on each default SG.

checks.title: Manual: enable AWS Config in all in-scope regions
checks.audit: For each region: 'aws configservice describe-configuration-recorders' should return a recorder, and 'aws configservice describe-configuration-recorder-status' should show recording=true.
checks.rationale: AWS Config captures point-in-time resource state for compliance and forensics.
checks.remediation: Enable AWS Config via Console > Config or the multi-region StackSet template.

checks.title: Manual: enable GuardDuty in all in-scope regions
checks.audit: For each region: 'aws guardduty list-detectors' should return at least one detector and 'aws guardduty get-detector --detector-id <id>' Status=ENABLED.
checks.rationale: GuardDuty is the baseline AWS threat-detection signal source.
checks.remediation: Enable via Console > GuardDuty or aws guardduty create-detector --enable.

checks.title: Manual: enable KMS customer-managed key rotation
checks.audit: For each CMK with KeyManager=CUSTOMER, run 'aws kms get-key-rotation-status'. Confirm KeyRotationEnabled=true for symmetric encryption keys.
checks.rationale: Annual rotation reduces blast radius if a CMK is compromised.
checks.remediation: aws kms enable-key-rotation --key-id <id>.

checks.title: IAM password policy prevents reuse of the last 24 passwords
checks.rationale: Password history prevents users from cycling back to a known credential.
checks.remediation: aws iam update-account-password-policy --password-reuse-prevention 24.

checks.title: IAM password policy expires passwords within 90 days
checks.rationale: Bounding console password age limits the lifetime of a leaked credential.
checks.remediation: aws iam update-account-password-policy --max-password-age 90.

checks.title: Manual: all IAM users with console access have MFA enabled
checks.audit: Generate the credential report ('aws iam generate-credential-report' then 'aws iam get-credential-report'). Confirm every row with password_enabled=true has mfa_active=true.
checks.rationale: Console users without MFA are a primary account-takeover vector.
checks.remediation: Enforce MFA via an IAM policy condition (aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent) and enroll each user.

checks.title: Manual: IAM access keys are rotated within 90 days
checks.audit: From the credential report, confirm access_key_1_last_rotated / access_key_2_last_rotated are within 90 days for all active keys.
checks.rationale: Long-lived access keys are a top breach vector when leaked in code or logs.
checks.remediation: Rotate keys on a schedule; prefer IAM roles / Identity Center over long-lived keys.

checks.title: CloudTrail is integrated with CloudWatch Logs
checks.rationale: CloudWatch Logs integration enables real-time metric filters and alarms on CloudTrail events.
checks.remediation: aws cloudtrail update-trail --name <name> --cloud-watch-logs-log-group-arn <arn> --cloud-watch-logs-role-arn <role>.

checks.title: CloudTrail logs are encrypted at rest with a KMS key
checks.rationale: SSE-KMS protects audit logs from unauthorized reads and supports key-based access control.
checks.remediation: aws cloudtrail update-trail --name <name> --kms-key-id <cmk-arn>.

checks.title: No security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 to SSH (port 22)
checks.command: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=ip-permission.from-port,Values=22 Name=ip-permission.cidr,Values=0.0.0.0/0 --query 'SecurityGroups | length(@)' --output text 2>/dev/null
checks.rationale: Internet-exposed SSH is a top initial-access vector.
checks.remediation: Restrict the rule to specific CIDRs or use SSM Session Manager for admin access.

checks.title: No security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 to RDP (port 3389)
checks.command: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=ip-permission.from-port,Values=3389 Name=ip-permission.cidr,Values=0.0.0.0/0 --query 'SecurityGroups | length(@)' --output text 2>/dev/null
checks.rationale: Internet-exposed RDP is heavily targeted by brute-force and ransomware actors.
checks.remediation: Restrict the rule to specific CIDRs or use SSM Session Manager / a bastion.

checks.title: VPC flow logs are enabled
checks.rationale: Flow logs provide network telemetry for investigation and anomaly detection.
checks.remediation: Enable VPC Flow Logs to CloudWatch Logs or S3 for each VPC.

checks.title: EBS encryption by default is enabled
checks.rationale: Default EBS encryption ensures new volumes/snapshots are encrypted without per-resource action.
checks.remediation: aws ec2 enable-ebs-encryption-by-default (per region).

checks.title: Manual: S3 buckets deny non-TLS (insecure transport) access
checks.audit: For each bucket, review the bucket policy for a Deny on aws:SecureTransport=false. Confirm cleartext HTTP access is rejected.
checks.rationale: Without an explicit deny, objects can be fetched over plain HTTP.
checks.remediation: Add a bucket policy statement: Effect=Deny when aws:SecureTransport is false.
